Combined with the previously accepted strict upper range, every 2q<=d<3q is excluded. In the original simultaneous inverse-row model, Delta(3q,q)>sqrt(2/3), with inherited quantitative composition Delta(3q,q)^2>=2/3+1/[30q(2q)^(2q-3)].

Inherited sparse-column sharp Weyl-defect theorem retains 1<=s<N, and commutator bounds retain their architecture-specific fixed-common-frame restrictions; single-neighborhood sharpness is not exact support-union or global uniform-row-sparsity sharpness.

Scalar inverse-defect corollaries retain integer s>=1; at s=0 invertibility forces full-rank defect and only the zero universal lower bound. No finite-field operator-norm transfer or free preparation/SVD/output costs are inferred.

For complex unitary U, 0<=r<t=|I| and d=t-r, the class of invertible M with rank(M^-1[I,J^c])<=r is empty if d>|J|. Otherwise its infimum distance to U is sqrt(1-sigma_d(U[J,I])^2), attained iff sigma_d>0. At sigma_d=0 every feasible error is >1 and the infimum is 1. If r>=t the constraint is automatic and zero error is attainable. All other entries remain unrestricted.

The bounded one-neighborhood comparison is complete: Lang Lemma 3.3 supplies the block-truncation/invertibility mechanism, with the general-unitary positive-rank deduction stated separately; Li-Lim Section 2.1 is a qualified Frobenius/invertibility nonmatch. This is not global uniform-row-sparsity sharpness, and historical priority remains unresolved.

The earlier complete N=2q degree set {1,2,q,2q}, q odd prime; for primes p<q, N=pq has degrees below q exactly {1,p}, and excludes (p-1)q<d<pq. These are degree-existence results, not classifications of every support.

The proper inverse-row equality-mask criterion includes all floor minimizers and strict infimum separation without a mask. Proper divisor d|N gives Delta(N,N-d)=sqrt(d/N); prime p is sharp only at s=p-1.

For every N>=4, codimension-three sharpness holds exactly when 3 divides N; weight-three equality masks have their separately proved full 3-by-3 block/four-congruence classification. This special theorem does not restore a universal full-block reduction.

Even half-density Delta(2m,m)=1/sqrt(2), with condition-one witness and exact m inverse-row/column nonzeros; singleton Delta(N,1)>sqrt(1-1/N) for N>=3, and the attained Delta(3,1)=sqrt(3)/2 with condition-one witness and singular values 1/2.

Earlier no-mask squared-gap s^6/[2^22 N^10 d^(2 phi(N)-2)], the sharper radical stability inequality, the improved 1/[10 N d^(phi(N)-1)] bound, the codimension-two 1/(5N^3) bound for odd N>=3, and codimension-three 1/(30N^3) bound for N>=4 with 3 not dividing N remain accepted in their proper domains N>=2, 1<=s<N, d=N-s.
For excluded N=2q weights the existing no-mask composition is Delta^2>=d/(2q)+1/[20q d^(q-2)]; the new N=3q composition is likewise inherited, not an optimal-gap-rate theorem.

Original inverse-support floor sqrt(1-s/N); architecture-specific rank-commutator floor cos((2 floor(r/2)+1)pi/(2N)); sharp sparse-column Weyl defect 2sin(pi/[2(s+1)]) only for 1<=s<N. Fourier commutator rank is N for even N and N-1 for odd N.

Stable inverse defect with M^-1=B+E, rank(E)<=r, |I|=t>r, J the union of B-row supports and d=t-r: error squared >=1-sigma_d(U[J,I])^2>=max(0,1-t|J|/[N(t-r)]). The singular-value inequality is unitary-general; the explicit Frobenius estimate uses Fourier flatness. Local forbidden-block rank refinement and the broad one-sided parity cutoff N/4 when 4 divides N remain accepted.

Source lineage retained: the historical Phase20 sparse/commutator audit; classical inverse-submatrix nullity, spectral approximation/minimax, and the completed Lang Lemma 3.3/Li-Lim Section 2.1 qualified comparison. None establishes worldwide priority.

The equality-mask construction of the original matrix M=(s/N)(A*)^-1 may be dense and requires a paid inverse/solve. Its general condition envelope is (1+a)/(1-a) in the inherited notation, not condition number one; condition-one claims are limited to their separately proved witnesses. Quantitative no-mask bounds add no condition-number restriction, attained-optimum assumption or compactness premise.

attribution: The previously unaccepted endpoint lead supplied the proof architecture; the accepted endpoint argument was independently derived and independently reviewed. No independent-discovery claim is made.

preserved: For characteristic-zero even N=2h>=4 and the fixed common-Weyl grammar T^N=-I, the accepted chirp-moment construction has h<=Qmin<=h+1 legal ordinary distinct nonzero nodes avoiding alpha^N=-1; algebraic extensions and their costs are allowed and charged, and zero residues may be retained or omitted.

The original finite-parameter pencil zP_h+tP_(h-1) has a legal choice among t=1,...,4h, by the separate repeated-root and forbidden-node bad-parameter counts. Consecutive coprimality alone does not establish P_h squarefreeness.

The accepted large-parameter family t_N=2^(10N^3+2) retains its all-embedding legality, explicit radius/separation/nonpole/derivative/Vandermonde/weight/residue bounds, old exhaustive preparation bound 2^[O(p+N^7)], and severe unscaled condition lower bound kappa_2(V)>=2^(2N^4). The old exhaustive algorithm remains a valid historical construction even though the new route improves its preparation upper bound.

The separate accepted compact rational family takes the least legal t in {1/(2N),...,1}, yields h+1 legal roots and unscaled kappa_2(V)<=2^(2N^3), with p+O(N^3)-bit approximations and 2^[O(p+N^3)] preparation. This is a distinct quantitative family, not polynomial conditioning.

The compact-family approximate whole-bank query retains its paid Karatsuba negacyclic O(N^log2(3)) exact-rational operation bound including address/dispatch and outputs, and O(N^log2(3)[N^2(p+N^3)+b]^2) query bit bound for b-bit dyadic inputs with relative error below 2^-p.

The large-t family query remains O(N^2) exact-rational operations and O(N^6(p+b+N^7)^2) bit work, separately from preparation. Paid endpoint diagonals, signed-wrap recurrence, normalization, all branches and outputs are included; the zero input is handled separately.
The accepted h+1 construction was already effective algebraically. Neither the earlier explicit family nor the new polynomial route is a first-computability or first-general-moment-theory claim.
